1660	        dict[int, list[str]],
1661	        dict[tuple[int, str], list[tuple[str | None, str | _SlicedArg | None]] | None],
1662	    ]:
1663	        """Return the transitive JIT dep graph rooted at this function.
1664	
1665	        The graph is computed lazily on first access and cached for the
1666	        lifetime of this ``JITFunction``. Returns:
1667	
1668	        - ``deps_topo``: every reachable dep in leaf-first topological order
1669	          (deduplicated by underlying Python function identity). The entry
1670	          function is NOT included.
1671	        - ``callers_by_dep_id``: for each dep, the list of Python functions
1672	          whose bodies contain a call site to it. Recorded in DFS-discovery
1673	          order; deduplicated within each list. The entry has no caller and
1674	          does not appear as a key.
1675	
1676	          Tensor / scalar metadata for a shared dep is still resolved
1677	          through the first-recorded caller — call sites in other branches
1678	          must agree on shapes/dtypes (otherwise one specialization would
1679	          have to differ from another, which the one-context-per-function
1680	          design doesn't support).
1681	        - ``callees_by_func_id``: for each function (entry + every reached
1682	          dep), the names of JIT deps it directly calls. Used to set each
1683	          context's ``dep_names`` so the body transformer rewrites nested
1684	          dep calls into the ``self.<dep>(...)`` form required by
1685	          multi-function ``@pl.program``.
1686	        - ``call_args_cache``: ``(id(caller_func), dep_name)`` → unified
1687	          call-site arg list (see ``_extract_call_args_for_dep``) or
1688	          ``None`` if the call site isn't found. Cached so metadata
1689	          resolution doesn't re-walk caller ASTs on every JIT call.
1690	        """
1691	        if self._dep_graph is None:
1692	            deps_topo: list[JITFunction] = []
1693	            seen: set[int] = set()
1694	            callers_by_dep_id: dict[int, list[Any]] = {}
1695	            callees_by_func_id: dict[int, list[str]] = {}
1696	            call_args_cache: dict[
1697	                tuple[int, str], list[tuple[str | None, str | _SlicedArg | None]] | None
1698	            ] = {}
1699	
1700	            def visit(func: Any, caller_func_type: str) -> None:
1701	                direct = _discover_deps(func, caller_func_type)
1702	                callees_by_func_id[id(func)] = [d.__name__ for d in direct]
1703	                for dep in direct:
1704	                    # Key everything off ``id(dep._func)`` (the underlying
1705	                    # Python function) — same key the downstream helpers
1706	                    # use, and stable across multiple wrapper objects for
1707	                    # the same source function.
1708	                    callers = callers_by_dep_id.setdefault(id(dep._func), [])
1709	                    if func not in callers:
1710	                        callers.append(func)
1711	                    # Memoise per-(caller, dep) call-site args once.
1712	                    cache_key = (id(func), dep.__name__)
1713	                    if cache_key not in call_args_cache:
1714	                        call_args_cache[cache_key] = _extract_call_args_for_dep(func, dep.__name__)
1715	                    if id(dep._func) in seen:
1716	                        continue
1717	                    # Mark before recursing — this also serves as a cycle
1718	                    # guard (a self-recursive JIT function is unsupported
1719	                    # but won't loop forever here).
1720	                    seen.add(id(dep._func))
1721	                    visit(dep._func, dep._func_type)
1722	                    deps_topo.append(dep)
1723	
1724	            visit(self._func, self._func_type)
1725	            self._dep_graph = (
1726	                deps_topo,
1727	                callers_by_dep_id,
1728	                callees_by_func_id,
1729	                call_args_cache,
1730	            )
1731	        return self._dep_graph
1732	
1733	    def _get_deps(self) -> list[JITFunction]:
1734	        """Return all transitively-reachable JIT deps in leaf-first order."""
1735	        return self._get_dep_graph()[0]
1736	
1737	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1738	    # Source hash (includes all dep sources; lazily computed after deps found)
1739	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1740	
1741	    def _external_source_paths(self) -> list[str]:
1742	        """Absolute paths of the C++ source(s) backing an external kernel dep."""
1743	        return [p for p in (self._external_aic_source, self._external_aiv_source) if p is not None]
1744	
1745	    def _get_source_hash(self) -> str:
1746	        deps = self._get_deps()
1747	        # External kernel .cpp files are mutable on disk, unlike the (fixed once
1748	        # loaded) Python source. When any extern dep is present, recompute the
1749	        # hash on every lookup so an edited kernel is picked up even within a
1750	        # long-lived process; otherwise cache it.
1751	        has_extern = any(d._func_type == "extern" for d in deps)
1752	        if self._source_hash is not None and not has_extern:
1753	            return self._source_hash
1754	        sources = [inspect.getsource(self._func)]
1755	        for dep in deps:
1756	            if dep._func_type == "extern":
1757	                # The implementation and launch ABI both affect the artifact.
1758	                # Include the quoted-include closure so editing a sibling .cce
1759	                # invalidates the cache even when the entry .cpp is unchanged.
1760	                sources.append(
1761	                    external_source_digest(
1762	                        dep._external_source_paths(),
1763	                        metadata=(
1764	                            inspect.getsource(dep._func),
1765	                            dep.__name__,
1766	                            dep._external_core_type or "",
1767	                            str(dep._external_dual_aiv_dispatch),
1768	                            *(f"include_dir:{path}" for path in dep._external_include_dirs),
1769	                        ),
1770	                        include_dirs=dep._external_include_dirs,
1771	                    )
1772	                )
1773	            else:
1774	                sources.append(inspect.getsource(dep._func))
1775	        source_hash = compute_source_hash(sources)
1776	        if not has_extern:
1777	            self._source_hash = source_hash
1778	        return source_hash
1779	
1780	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1781	    # Parameter introspection
1782	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1783	
1784	    def _param_names(self) -> list[str]:
1785	        return [p for p in inspect.signature(self._func).parameters if p != "self"]
1786	
1787	    def _bind_args(
1788	        self, args: tuple[Any, ...], kwargs: dict[str, Any]
1789	    ) -> tuple[
1790	        list[str],
1791	        dict[str, Any],
1792	        dict[str, TensorMeta],
1793	        dict[str, int | float | bool],
1794	        dict[str, DataType],
1795	        dict[int, dict[str, dict[int, DynDim]]],
1796	    ]:
1797	        """Bind *args/**kwargs to param names and classify into tensor/scalar metadata.
1798	
1799	        Tensor metas carry ``DynDim`` entries for every param dim that is
1800	        either declared dynamic at this function (``bind_dynamic`` / annotation
1801	        ``pl.dynamic()``) **or** cascaded up from a dep's declarations.
1802	        Cascading happens during ``_compute_per_func_dyndim_maps`` so the cache
1803	        key reflects every dynamic dim reachable through the dep graph — two
1804	        calls with different runtime extents reuse the same compilation.
1805	
1806	        Returns the per-function DynDim map alongside the entry metadata so
1807	        downstream specialization (``_resolve_dep_call_metadata``) can pull
1808	        each dep's effective map without recomputing.
1809	        """
1810	        param_names = self._param_names()
1811	        sig = inspect.signature(self._func)
1812	        try:
1813	            bound = sig.bind(*args, **kwargs)
1814	            bound.apply_defaults()
1815	        except TypeError as e:
1816	            raise TypeError(f"@pl.jit function '{self.__name__}': {e}") from e
1817	
1818	        arguments = dict(bound.arguments)
1819	
1820	        deps, callers_by_id, _, call_args_cache = self._get_dep_graph()
1821	        per_func_dyn_maps = _compute_per_func_dyndim_maps(
1822	            self._func, param_names, deps, callers_by_id, call_args_cache
1823	        )
1824	        entry_dyn_map = per_func_dyn_maps[id(self._func)]
1825	        # A layout has no runtime counterpart on a torch tensor, so it comes
1826	        # from the annotation even on this path.
1827	        param_layouts = _param_layouts(self._func, self.__name__)
1828	        tensor_meta: dict[str, TensorMeta] = {}
1829	        scalar_values: dict[str, int | float | bool] = {}
1830	        scalar_dtypes: dict[str, DataType] = {}
1831	
1832	        from pypto.language.typing.scalar import RUNTIME  # noqa: PLC0415
1833	
1834	        for name, value in arguments.items():
1835	            # ``pl.RUNTIME`` is a compile-time marker, not a value. This path
1836	            # binds real arguments (dispatch, or sample-argument compile), where
1837	            # an unrecognized object would otherwise slip through the
1838	            # int/float/bool filter below and fail much later with an opaque
1839	            # "must be real number" from the runtime. Note ``apply_defaults()``
1840	            # above materializes a ``= pl.RUNTIME`` signature default, so a plain
1841	            # ``kernel(a, c)`` call reaches here too.
1842	            if value is RUNTIME:
1843	                raise TypeError(
1844	                    f"@pl.jit function '{self.__name__}': parameter '{name}' received "
1845	                    f"pl.RUNTIME, which is a compile-time marker rather than a value. It is "
1846	                    f"only accepted by annotation-driven signature mode — call compile() or "
1847	                    f"lower() with no tensor arguments and pass it by keyword, e.g. "
1848	                    f"{self.__name__}.compile({name}=pl.RUNTIME). To run the kernel, pass "
1849	                    f"'{name}' its actual value."
1850	                )
1851	            if _is_tensor(value):
1852	                tensor_meta[name] = _extract_tensor_meta(
1853	                    value, entry_dyn_map.get(name), param_layouts.get(name)
1854	                )
1855	            elif isinstance(value, (int, float, bool)):
1856	                scalar_values[name] = value
1857	
1858	        return param_names, arguments, tensor_meta, scalar_values, scalar_dtypes, per_func_dyn_maps
1859	
1860	    def _bind_args_from_signature(
1861	        self, kwargs: dict[str, Any]
1862	    ) -> tuple[
1863	        list[str],
1864	        dict[str, Any],
1865	        dict[str, TensorMeta],
1866	        dict[str, int | float | bool],
1867	        dict[str, DataType],
1868	        dict[int, dict[str, dict[int, DynDim]]],
1869	    ]:
1870	        """Derive the same metadata as ``_bind_args``, but from the kernel's
1871	        own parameter annotations — no tensor arguments required.
1872	
1873	        Used by [`lower`][pypto.language.JITFunction.lower] and
1874	        [`compile`][pypto.language.JITFunction.compile] in annotation-driven signature mode. Each tensor
1875	        parameter's ``pl.Tensor[[...], dtype]`` annotation supplies the shape/dtype contract directly: static
1876	        dims are annotation integers, while dynamic dims (``pl.dynamic`` / ``bind_dynamic``) are marked
1877	        dynamic and given a placeholder extent. Dynamic dimensions lower to runtime ``pl.tensor.dim`` reads
1878	        and, on the compiled path, collapse to ``None`` in the cache key.
1879	
1880	        Scalar parameters carry no value in the signature, so their values must
1881	        come from ``kwargs`` (or a signature default). A literal is specialized
1882	        into the artifact; ``pl.RUNTIME`` instead leaves the parameter
1883	        unspecialized — it is omitted from ``scalar_values`` (and therefore from
1884	        the cache key) and survives into the generated program as a real
1885	        ``pl.Scalar`` parameter, exactly like a dynamic dim extent.
1886	
1887	        Raises:
1888	            TypeError: if a tensor parameter has a bare ``pl.Tensor`` annotation
1889	                (no shape to read), or a scalar parameter has no supplied value.
1890	        """
1891	        from pypto.language.typing.dynamic import DynVar  # noqa: PLC0415
1892	        from pypto.language.typing.scalar import Scalar  # noqa: PLC0415
1893	        from pypto.language.typing.tensor import Tensor  # noqa: PLC0415
1894	
1895	        param_names = self._param_names()
1896	        sig = inspect.signature(self._func)
1897	
1898	        # Namespace for resolving string annotations (``from __future__ import
1899	        # annotations``): the function's globals merged with its closure free-vars,
1900	        # so an annotation referencing an enclosing scope (e.g. a ``pl.dynamic`` /
1901	        # constant defined in an outer function) resolves. We ``eval`` each string
1902	        # annotation directly rather than via ``typing.get_type_hints`` because the
1903	        # latter runs ``_type_check`` on the result, which rejects our custom
1904	        # ``Tensor`` / ``Scalar`` instance annotations on Python 3.10.
1905	        ann_ns: dict[str, Any] | None = None
1906	        if any(isinstance(p.annotation, str) for n, p in sig.parameters.items() if n != "self"):
1907	            ann_ns = _func_name_lookup(self._func)
1908	
1909	        deps, callers_by_id, _, call_args_cache = self._get_dep_graph()
1910	        per_func_dyn_maps = _compute_per_func_dyndim_maps(
1911	            self._func, param_names, deps, callers_by_id, call_args_cache
1912	        )
1913	        entry_dyn_map = per_func_dyn_maps[id(self._func)]
1914	
1915	        tensor_meta: dict[str, TensorMeta] = {}
1916	        scalar_values: dict[str, int | float | bool] = {}
1917	        scalar_dtypes: dict[str, DataType] = {}
1918	
1919	        for name in param_names:
1920	            param = sig.parameters[name]
1921	            annotation = param.annotation
1922	            if isinstance(annotation, str) and ann_ns is not None:
1923	                try:
1924	                    # Trusted input: the kernel's own annotation source, evaluated
1925	                    # in its own globals+closure namespace (same as Python would).
1926	                    annotation = eval(annotation, ann_ns)  # noqa: S307
1927	                except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - leave as string; handled below as "cannot infer"
1928	                    pass
1929	
1930	            # A bare ``pl.Tensor`` is the Tensor *class* itself (no shape);
1931	            # ``pl.Tensor[[...], dtype]`` is a Tensor *instance* carrying
1932	            # shape/dtype. ``pl.Out[...]``/``pl.InOut[...]`` unwrap to their
1933	            # inner type, so both directions flow through the instance branch.
1934	            bare_msg = (
1935	                f"@pl.jit function '{self.__name__}': cannot specialize from the signature "
1936	                f"because parameter '{name}' has a bare 'pl.Tensor' annotation with no shape. "
1937	                f"Give it a full 'pl.Tensor[[...], dtype]' annotation, or pass sample tensors "
1938	                f"to lower(*sample_tensors) or compile(*sample_tensors)."
1939	            )
1940	            if isinstance(annotation, Tensor):
1941	                if annotation.shape is None or annotation.dtype is None:
1942	                    raise TypeError(bare_msg)
1943	                tensor_meta[name] = _signature_tensor_meta(
1944	                    annotation,
1945	                    annotation.dtype,
1946	                    entry_dyn_map.get(name, {}),
1947	                    DynVar,
1948	                    param_name=name,
1949	                    func_name=self.__name__,
1950	                )
1951	                continue
1952	            if isinstance(annotation, type) and issubclass(annotation, Tensor):
1953	                raise TypeError(bare_msg)
1954	
1955	            # Scalar-like annotation: pl.Scalar[dtype] or a bare DataType.
1956	            scalar_dtype = annotation.dtype if isinstance(annotation, Scalar) else None
1957	            if scalar_dtype is None and isinstance(annotation, DataType):
1958	                scalar_dtype = annotation
1959	            if scalar_dtype is not None:
1960	                value = _signature_scalar_value(self.__name__, name, param, kwargs)
1961	                # ``pl.RUNTIME`` -> no ``scalar_values`` entry. The specializer only
1962	                # substitutes names present in ``scalar_values``, so the parameter
1963	                # stays symbolic in the generated program; it also drops out of the
1964	                # cache key, so one artifact serves every runtime value.
1965	                if value is not None:
1966	                    scalar_values[name] = value
1967	                scalar_dtypes[name] = scalar_dtype
1968	                continue
1969	
1970	            # Unknown / unannotated parameter — cannot infer without a value.
1971	            raise TypeError(
1972	                f"@pl.jit function '{self.__name__}': cannot infer parameter '{name}' from the "
1973	                f"signature (annotation: {annotation!r}). Annotate it as a shaped 'pl.Tensor' / "
1974	                f"'pl.Scalar[dtype]', or pass sample values to lower(*sample_args) or "
1975	                f"compile(*sample_args)."
1976	            )
1977	
1978	        # Signature mode has no tensor sample arguments. Preserve supplied
1979	        # scalar values in the same arguments mapping returned by _bind_args.
1980	        arguments = dict(scalar_values)
1981	        return param_names, arguments, tensor_meta, scalar_values, scalar_dtypes, per_func_dyn_maps
1982	
1983	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1984	    # Call
1985	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1986	
1987	    def _resolve_specialization(
1988	        self,
1989	        args: tuple[Any, ...],
1990	        kwargs: dict[str, Any],
1991	        allow_signature_mode: bool = False,
1992	    ) -> tuple[_Specialization, Any | None]:
1993	        """Bind signature or sample arguments and consume the ``RunConfig``.
1994	
1995	        Shared by [`lower`][pypto.language.JITFunction.lower], ``__call__``, and
1996	        [`compile`][pypto.language.JITFunction.compile].
1997	
1998	        When ``allow_signature_mode`` is set and no positional args are given,
1999	        the shape/dtype contract is read from the kernel's own annotations via
2000	        ``_bind_args_from_signature``. ``__call__`` never enables this
2001	        because on-device dispatch needs real tensors.
2002	
2003	        Returns:
2004	            The specialization metadata and the consumed ``RunConfig``.
2005	        """
2006	        # Extract RunConfig without mutating *kwargs* — although the caller's
2007	        # ``**kwargs`` dict is normally owned by Python at this scope, building
2008	        # a fresh dict is the same cost and removes the ambiguity for readers
2009	        # who don't track the calling convention.
2010	        run_config = kwargs.get("config")
2011	        if "config" in kwargs:
2012	            kwargs = {k: v for k, v in kwargs.items() if k != "config"}
2013	
2014	        # Annotation-driven signature mode (lower() and compile()) reads shapes
2015	        # from annotations, but ONLY when no tensor values were supplied —
2016	        # positionally OR by keyword. Keyword tensor samples (``lower(a=x)`` or
2017	        # ``compile(a=x)``) must still bind through ``_bind_args``/``sig.bind``;
2018	        # scalar/config kwargs do not block signature mode.
2019	        signature_mode = allow_signature_mode and not args and not any(_is_tensor(v) for v in kwargs.values())
2020	        if signature_mode:
2021	            param_names, arguments, tensor_meta, scalar_values, scalar_dtypes, per_func_dyn = (
2022	                self._bind_args_from_signature(kwargs)
2023	            )
2024	        else:
2025	            param_names, arguments, tensor_meta, scalar_values, scalar_dtypes, per_func_dyn = self._bind_args(
2026	                args, kwargs
2027	            )
2028	
2029	        return (
2030	            _Specialization(
2031	                param_names,
2032	                arguments,
2033	                tensor_meta,
2034	                scalar_values,
2035	                scalar_dtypes,
2036	                per_func_dyn,
2037	            ),
2038	            run_config,
2039	        )
2040	
2041	    def _resolve_compiled(
2042	        self,
2043	        args: tuple[Any, ...],
2044	        kwargs: dict[str, Any],
2045	        allow_signature_mode: bool = False,
2046	    ) -> tuple[Any, list[Any], Any | None]:
2047	        """Look up or build a specialized CompiledProgram.
2048	
2049	        Shared by ``__call__`` (which then dispatches) and [`compile`][pypto.language.JITFunction.compile]
2050	        (which then returns the CompiledProgram). Cache keys include all inputs
2051	        that affect the generated artifact.
2052	
2053	        Returns:
2054	            ``(compiled, ordered_args, run_config)`` where ``ordered_args``
2055	            follows the decorated function's declared parameter order.
2056	        """
2057	        import pypto.language as pl  # noqa: PLC0415
2058	
2059	        specialization, run_config = self._resolve_specialization(
2060	            args,
2061	            kwargs,
2062	            allow_signature_mode=allow_signature_mode,
2063	        )
2064	
2065	        # Compile-side knobs (strategy, dump_passes, ...) come from the
2066	        # RunConfig. Forwarding them lets a @pl.jit kernel honour the same
2067	        # compile options as a direct ir.compile(program, ...) call.
2068	        compile_kwargs = _run_config_compile_kwargs(run_config) if run_config is not None else {}
2069	
2070	        # Build cache key. Platform and strategy are included so artifacts
2071	        # compiled for different targets or optimization strategies never
2072	        # collide in the same cache. With no RunConfig the strategy is
2073	        # normalized to ir.compile()'s own default so the key holds the
2074	        # effective strategy rather than a None sentinel.

"""@pl.jit decorator implementation.

Public API
----------
    # Single-function: one @jit entry with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP) scope
    @pl.jit
    def kernel(a: pl.Tensor, b: pl.Tensor, c: pl.Out[pl.Tensor]):
        with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP):
            M, N = a.shape
            ...

    # Multi-function: @jit entry + one or more sub-function deps. Three flavours:
    @pl.jit.incore
    def sub_kernel(a: pl.Tensor, c: pl.Out[pl.Tensor]):     # FunctionType.InCore
        ...

    @pl.jit.inline
    def util(a: pl.Tensor, c: pl.Out[pl.Tensor]):           # FunctionType.Inline
        ...                                                 # spliced at call site

    @pl.jit.opaque
    def opaque_util(a: pl.Tensor, c: pl.Out[pl.Tensor]):    # FunctionType.Opaque
        for i in pl.parallel(...):                          # may wrap orchestration
            with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP):          # loops + pl.at scopes
                ...

    @pl.jit
    def entry(a: pl.Tensor, c: pl.Out[pl.Tensor]):
        c = sub_kernel(a, c)   # dep discovered automatically (any of incore/inline/opaque)
        return c

JITFunction.__call__ flow
-------------------------
1. Lazily discover deps (incore/inline/opaque) from entry's globals (once).
2. Classify args: tensor vs scalar.
3. Extract TensorMeta from torch.Tensor arguments.
4. Scan entry + dep ASTs for bind_dynamic declarations.
5. Build CacheKey (dynamic dims → None in shape tuple).
6. Cache hit  → execute cached CompiledProgram on device → return result.
7. Cache miss → specialize (entry + deps) → pl.parse() → ir.compile() → cache → execute → return.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import copy
import functools
import inspect
import os
import re
import textwrap
from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
from typing import Any, NamedTuple

from pypto._external_source import external_source_digest
from pypto.backend._ptoas_locate import find_ptoas_binary
from pypto.pypto_core import DataType
from pypto.pypto_core import ir as _ir
from pypto.pypto_core import passes as _passes

from .cache import CacheKey, compute_source_hash, make_cache_key
from .specializer import (
    DynDim,
    ShapeDim,
    SpecializeContext,
    Specializer,
    TensorMeta,
    _classify_params,
    _collect_annotation_dynamic_dims,
    _collect_dynvar_names,
    build_specialize_context,
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Error message rewriting for JIT compilation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _rewrite_jit_error(exc: Exception, rename_map: dict[str, str]) -> Exception:
    """Replace internal alpha-renamed aliases (e.g. ``x_v1``) with the user's
    original variable name (``x``) in the exception message.

    Uses word-boundary matching to avoid partial replacements (e.g. replacing
    ``max_v1`` when the alias is ``x_v1``). Sorts aliases longest-first so
    longer aliases are matched before any shorter prefix aliases.
    """
    if not rename_map:
        return exc
    msg = str(exc)
    for alias in sorted(rename_map, key=len, reverse=True):
        original = rename_map[alias]
        msg = re.sub(rf"\b{re.escape(alias)}\b", original, msg)
    if msg == str(exc):
        return exc
    # Use copy.copy to preserve all exception fields (span, hint, note,
    # source_lines for ParserError subclasses) then patch the message.
    try:
        new_exc = copy.copy(exc)
        new_exc.args = (msg,)
        if hasattr(new_exc, "message"):
            object.__setattr__(new_exc, "message", msg)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        # If copy fails (e.g. non-standard __init__), fall back to plain Exception.
        new_exc = Exception(msg)
    return new_exc


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# torch-optional dtype conversion
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Sentinel list: empty means not yet loaded; [None] means torch unavailable;
# [torch_module] means torch is loaded.
_TORCH_CACHE: list[Any] = []
_TORCH_DTYPE_MAP: dict[Any, DataType] = {}


def _get_torch() -> Any:
    """Return the torch module, or None if not installed. Result is cached."""
    if not _TORCH_CACHE:
        try:
            import torch  # noqa: PLC0415

            _TORCH_CACHE.append(torch)
            _TORCH_DTYPE_MAP.update(
                {
                    torch.float16: DataType.FP16,
                    torch.float32: DataType.FP32,
                    torch.bfloat16: DataType.BF16,
                    torch.int8: DataType.INT8,
                    torch.int16: DataType.INT16,
                    torch.int32: DataType.INT32,
                    torch.int64: DataType.INT64,
                    torch.uint8: DataType.UINT8,
                    torch.bool: DataType.BOOL,
                }
            )
            # Optional low-precision MX dtypes (PyTorch 2.1+/2.3+/2.7+); required
            # for MX DSL ST. float4_e2m1fn_x2 is the packed MXFP4 weight dtype.
            for _torch_name, _pto_dt in (
                ("float8_e4m3fn", DataType.FP8E4M3FN),
                ("float8_e5m2", DataType.FP8E5M2),
                ("float8_e8m0fnu", DataType.FP8E8M0),
                ("float4_e2m1fn_x2", DataType.FP4),
            ):
                _td = getattr(torch, _torch_name, None)
                if _td is not None:
                    _TORCH_DTYPE_MAP[_td] = _pto_dt

        except ImportError:
            _TORCH_CACHE.append(None)
    return _TORCH_CACHE[0]


def _torch_dtype_to_pypto(torch_dtype: Any) -> DataType:
    _get_torch()
    if torch_dtype not in _TORCH_DTYPE_MAP:
        raise TypeError(
            f"Unsupported torch dtype {torch_dtype}. "
            "Supported: float16, float32, bfloat16, int8/16/32/64, uint8, bool, "
            "float8_e4m3fn/e5m2/e8m0fnu, float4_e2m1fn_x2 (where torch supports them)."
        )
    return _TORCH_DTYPE_MAP[torch_dtype]


def _ptoas_available() -> bool:
    """Return True if the ptoas binary is available on this machine."""
    return find_ptoas_binary() is not None


def _is_tensor(obj: Any) -> bool:
    """Return True if obj is a torch.Tensor (without hard-importing torch)."""
    torch = _get_torch()
    if torch is None:
        return False
    return isinstance(obj, torch.Tensor)


def _build_tensor_meta(
    extents: Sequence[int],
    dtype: DataType,
    dyn_dims: dict[int, DynDim] | None = None,
    layout: _ir.TensorLayout | None = None,
) -> TensorMeta:
    """Build a ``TensorMeta`` from per-dim extents and a resolved dtype.

    ``dyn_dims`` maps ``dim_idx → DynDim`` for dims declared dynamic at this
    parameter (via ``bind_dynamic`` or an annotation-embedded ``pl.dynamic()``).
    The DynDim's ``static_bound`` is filled from the corresponding extent.
    Shared by the torch-tensor path (``_extract_tensor_meta``, extent = the
    real tensor dim) and the signature path (``JITFunction._bind_args_from_signature``,
    extent = the static annotation dim or a placeholder for dynamic dims).

    ``layout`` is the annotation's third slot. It never comes from a runtime
    tensor — a torch tensor carries no PyPTO layout — so both paths read it
    from the same place, the parameter's annotation.
    """
    dyn = dyn_dims or {}
    shape: list[ShapeDim] = []
    for i, d in enumerate(extents):
        extent = int(d)
        bound = dyn.get(i)
        if bound is None:
            shape.append(extent)
        else:
            shape.append(DynDim(name=bound.name, literal=bound.literal, static_bound=extent))
    return TensorMeta(shape=tuple(shape), dtype=dtype, layout=layout)


def _extract_tensor_meta(
    tensor: Any,
    dyn_dims: dict[int, DynDim] | None = None,
    layout: _ir.TensorLayout | None = None,
) -> TensorMeta:
    """Extract TensorMeta from a torch.Tensor (shape/dtype only — no data read).

    ``layout`` comes from the parameter's annotation, not the tensor: torch has
    no notion of a PyPTO layout, so the annotation is the only source.
    """
    dtype = _torch_dtype_to_pypto(tensor.dtype)
    extents = list(tensor.shape)
    if dtype == DataType.FP4:
        if not extents:
            raise TypeError("Packed torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2 tensors must have rank >= 1")
        if extents[-1] <= 0:
            raise TypeError(
                "Packed torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2 tensors require a positive runtime x2 carrier last "
                f"dimension; got shape {tuple(extents)}"
            )
        # Torch exposes one x2 carrier per byte. PyPTO IR and PTO-ISA count
        # logical FP4 nibbles, so expand only at this API boundary and keep the
        # storage shape out of TensorType/TileType.
        extents[-1] *= 2
    return _build_tensor_meta(extents, dtype, dyn_dims, layout)


def _resolve_annotation(annotation: Any, ann_ns: dict[str, Any] | None) -> Any:
    """Resolve one parameter annotation, evaluating the string form if needed.

    ``from __future__ import annotations`` in the *user's* module leaves every
    annotation as a string; ``ann_ns`` (from ``_func_name_lookup``) is the
    namespace to evaluate it in.

    Args:
        annotation: Raw ``inspect.Parameter.annotation``
        ann_ns: Namespace for string annotations, or None to leave them as-is

    Returns:
        The resolved annotation object, or the original string when it cannot
        be evaluated
    """
    if not isinstance(annotation, str) or ann_ns is None:
        return annotation
    try:
        # Trusted input: the kernel's own annotation source, evaluated in its
        # own globals+closure namespace (same as Python would).
        return eval(annotation, ann_ns)  # noqa: S307
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - leave as string; callers treat it as "cannot infer"
        return annotation


def _annotation_namespace(func: Any, sig: inspect.Signature) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Namespace for resolving ``func``'s string annotations, or None if unneeded."""
    if any(isinstance(p.annotation, str) for n, p in sig.parameters.items() if n != "self"):
        return _func_name_lookup(func)
    return None


def _annotation_layout(annotation: Any, param_name: str, func_name: str) -> _ir.TensorLayout | None:
    """Read the layout slot off an already-resolved tensor annotation.

    ``pl.Tensor[[...], dtype, pl.NZ]`` evaluates to a ``Tensor`` instance whose
    ``layout`` holds the third slot; the two-slot form leaves it None.

    Args:
        annotation: Resolved parameter annotation (any object — non-tensor
            annotations simply carry no layout)
        param_name: Parameter the annotation belongs to, for diagnostics
        func_name: Enclosing kernel name, for diagnostics

    Returns:
        The annotated layout, or None when the annotation declares none

    Raises:
        TypeError: If the slot holds a ``pl.TensorView`` — specialization has
            nowhere to carry it, and silently dropping it would mis-declare the
            parameter
    """
    layout = getattr(annotation, "layout", None)
    if layout is None or isinstance(layout, _ir.TensorLayout):
        return layout
    # ``Tensor.__getitem__`` routes any non-MemRef third element into ``layout``,
    # so a pl.TensorView(...) lands here. TensorMeta has no field for it, and a
    # dropped stride is silently wrong code — refuse instead. This is reachable
    # from the DN rejection's own migration hint, so the message has to be plain.
    raise TypeError(
        f"@pl.jit function {func_name!r}: parameter {param_name!r} annotates a "
        f"{type(layout).__name__} in its layout slot, which @pl.jit does not yet "
        f"support — it would be dropped and the parameter compiled as ND. Use a "
        f"plain layout (e.g. pl.MX_A_ZZ), or declare the kernel with @pl.function, "
        f"which resolves the annotation directly."
    )


def _param_layouts(func: Any, func_name: str) -> dict[str, _ir.TensorLayout]:
    """Map parameter name → annotated layout, for params that declare one.

    The torch-argument path derives shape and dtype from the passed tensors, so
    it never looks at annotations — but a layout has no runtime counterpart to
    read, making the annotation its only source. This recovers it. Also used to
    recover a dep function's own declarations, which no caller argument carries.

    Args:
        func: The Python function whose annotations to read
        func_name: Name to use in diagnostics

    Returns:
        Layout per parameter name; parameters without one are absent
    """
    try:
        sig = inspect.signature(func)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return {}
    ann_ns = _annotation_namespace(func, sig)

    layouts: dict[str, _ir.TensorLayout] = {}
    for name, param in sig.parameters.items():
        if name == "self":
            continue
        layout = _annotation_layout(_resolve_annotation(param.annotation, ann_ns), name, func_name)
        if layout is not None:
            layouts[name] = layout
    return layouts


def _signature_tensor_meta(
    annotation: Any,
    dtype: DataType,
    dyn_for_param: dict[int, DynDim],
    dynvar_cls: type,
    param_name: str = "",
    func_name: str = "",
) -> TensorMeta:
    """Build TensorMeta from a shaped ``pl.Tensor[[...], dtype]`` annotation.

    Static dims use the annotation integer; dynamic dims (``pl.dynamic`` /
    ``bind_dynamic``) get a placeholder extent because the specialized program
    remains extent-independent. ``dynvar_cls`` is the lazily-imported ``DynVar``
    type. ``param_name`` / ``func_name`` only feed diagnostics.
    """
    shape = annotation.shape
    extents = [
        1 if (i in dyn_for_param or isinstance(dim, dynvar_cls)) else int(dim) for i, dim in enumerate(shape)
    ]
    # Record annotation-only DynVars not already bound via bind_dynamic.
    dyn_dims = dict(dyn_for_param)
    for i, dim in enumerate(shape):
        if isinstance(dim, dynvar_cls) and i not in dyn_dims:
            dyn_dims[i] = DynDim(name=dim.name, literal=dim.name, static_bound=0)
    layout = _annotation_layout(annotation, param_name, func_name)
    return _build_tensor_meta(extents, dtype, dyn_dims, layout)


def _signature_scalar_value(
    func_name: str,
    name: str,
    param: inspect.Parameter,
    kwargs: dict[str, Any],
) -> int | float | bool | None:
    """Resolve a scalar parameter's value for signature-mode specialization.

    Value comes from ``kwargs`` (by param name) or the signature default; a
    scalar with neither is an error (the signature carries no value).

    Returns:
        The literal to specialize into the compiled artifact, or ``None`` when
        the caller passed ``pl.RUNTIME`` — the parameter then stays a runtime
        ``pl.Scalar`` in the generated program instead of being baked in.
    """
    from pypto.language.typing.scalar import RUNTIME  # noqa: PLC0415

    if name in kwargs:
        value = kwargs[name]
    elif param.default is not inspect.Parameter.empty:
        value = param.default
    else:
        raise TypeError(
            f"@pl.jit function '{func_name}': scalar parameter '{name}' has no value. When "
            f"specializing from annotations, pass scalar values as keyword arguments, e.g. "
            f"lower({name}=...) or compile({name}=...). Pass '{name}=pl.RUNTIME' instead to "
            f"leave it unspecialized (its value is supplied at dispatch)."
        )
    if value is RUNTIME:
        return None
    if not isinstance(value, (int, float, bool)):
        raise TypeError(
            f"@pl.jit function '{func_name}': scalar parameter '{name}' must be an int/float/bool "
            f"(specializes the value into the artifact) or pl.RUNTIME (leaves it unspecialized), "
            f"got {type(value).__name__}."
        )
    return value
